newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia not worried over secret deals at Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Estonia not worried over secret deals at Helsinki.

text.p: The Baltic state of Estonia, like neighbours Latvia and Lithuania nervously eyeing the Helsinki summit, does not believe deals will be made against the Balts' interests, Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said on Thursday.

Some Balts fear U.S. President Bill Clinton will strike a deal with Russian President Boris Yeltsin to allow the entry of Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic into NATO in return for guarantees the Balts and other former Soviet republics will not be admitted.
But Ilves told the newspaper Eesti Paevaleht he was confident such a deal would not be made.
"...I believe Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin are not meeting to discuss the future of Estonia or the Baltics," Ilves said.
"We should get over thinking the summit is about us. The main topic of the summit is U.S./Russian relations," he added.
Balts have well-founded suspicions of meetings between major powers where their future may be on the agenda.
They bitterly remember the 1939 Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact when Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union carved up the three nations.
Balts also recall the 1945 Yalta conference, when Britain, the U.S. and the Soviet Union settled the post-war map and left the Balts to Moscow although they were previously independent.
Ilves said he did not believe the U.S. would sacrifice the Baltic states for Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.

"...In Helsinki there will be no 3+3 agreement as has been claimed in some Baltic countries: that three eastern European nations will be let into NATO and for that the three Baltic states will be left for the Russians," Ilves said.
He said that if such a deal were made, it would make a mockery of the whole NATO expansion process.

"Something that would establish the role of the Baltic nations without the participation of the Baltic nations would obviously mean the collapse of the whole NATO expansion process in the U.S. Congress," Ilves said.
